metaData.title: A Practical Guide to AI Infra: How Large Models Perform Efficient Inference
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Based on an in-depth reading of the vLLM source code, this article uses Llama 3 as an example to systematically explain the complete efficient inference pipeline of large models, from Tokenize to Sampling, by tracing the tensor dimension changes at each step.
metaData.summary: This article summarizes the author's two months of spare-time deep dive into the vLLM source code. Focusing on Decoder-Only LLMs, and using Llama 3 as an example, it breaks down the complete inference pipeline from Tokenize, Embedding Lookup, Transformer Block (Attention and FFN) to LM Head and Sampling. The core highlight is that the author annotates the tensor dimension changes at each computational step and provides an in-depth explanation of how two key technologies, Continuous Batching and Paged Attention, improve inference efficiency. The article also explores the fundamental differences between the Prefill and Decode phases in terms of computation and memory access, and how FlashAttention breaks the memory wall through Online Softmax. Finally, it concludes that the MLP layer is compute-bound while the Attention layer is memory-bound, and includes a table of model configuration parameters and runtime variables, offering a solid introductory reference for AI Infra practitioners.

mainPoints.point: Continuous Batching shifts the scheduling granularity from the request level down to the token level, significantly boosting GPU utilization.
mainPoints.explanation: By scheduling at the token level, multiple requests can reuse model weights, transforming operations like QKV_Proj, O_Proj, and MLP from matrix-vector multiplications (GEMV) back into matrix multiplications (GEMM), thus amortizing the memory cost of loading weights.

mainPoints.point: Paged Attention manages KV Cache using a virtual page table mechanism, solving the memory fragmentation problem.
mainPoints.explanation: Similar to virtual memory in operating systems, Paged Attention allocates non-contiguous physical blocks for each request and uses a block table for indirect addressing, greatly improving GPU memory utilization. This is the foundation for supporting high-performance inference with Continuous Batching.

mainPoints.point: The Prefill phase is compute-bound, while the Decode phase is memory-bound.
mainPoints.explanation: The Prefill phase processes a large number of tokens, has high computational intensity, and is limited by Tensor Cores compute power. The Decode phase processes only one token at a time, requiring the transfer of a large amount of KV Cache and model weights from HBM, and is therefore limited by memory bandwidth.

mainPoints.point: FlashAttention breaks the memory wall through kernel fusion and the Online Softmax algorithm.
mainPoints.explanation: FlashAttention fuses Q-K dot product, Softmax, and multiplication by V into a single CUDA kernel, computing in blocks within SRAM. This avoids writing large intermediate matrices to HBM, significantly improving the performance of Attention computation.

keyQuotes: What if we could shift the scheduling granularity from the request level down to the token level? Congratulations, you've just invented continuous batching.

Should the KV Cache memory allocation for each request also be at the token level, instead of allocating all memory at once? What if we use an address array (block table) to manage the KV Cache addresses for each request? Congratulations, you've just invented Paged Attention.

Compared to OOM caused by memory fragmentation, sacrificing a small amount of memory bandwidth for a significant increase in overall system throughput is a worthwhile trade-off in the overall logic of LLM inference.
Don't rebuild from scratch; instead, learn the 'correction value' (Delta) based on the original. This is the physical foundation of the 'Scaling Law' in architecture.

From an inference perspective alone, the principles of large models are actually not that esoteric. The most difficult mathematical formula is probably RoPE. But there is so much to learn in AI Infra... It's endless.

relatedArticles.title: From Requirements to Deployment: A Comprehensive Leap in R&D Efficiency with Full AI Automation
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically explains how Tencent's audit team built a fully automated AI delivery platform to achieve end-to-end automation from requirements, design, development, testing to deployment, and shares its evolution path from L2 (human-machine collaboration) to L3 (full automation), along with core challenges, specific practices, and quantified benefits.

relatedArticles.title: Next-Generation Large Model Inference Network Architecture: How ZCube Effectively Breaks the Network Bottleneck?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Zhipu AI, XunYin Network, and Tsinghua University jointly proposed the ZCube networking architecture. By employing a flat topology and a hybrid single/multi-rail access method, it achieves a 33% cost reduction, over 15% throughput improvement, and a 40.6% reduction in TTFT P99 in a thousand-card inference cluster, effectively solving the structural network congestion problem in PD-separated inference.

relatedArticles.title: A Comprehensive Introduction to AI Infra: Understanding the Mathematics and Infra Optimization of Large Models
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the underlying logic of core operations such as RMSNorm, Softmax, and Causal Mask in large model inference from both mathematical principles and engineering optimization perspectives, revealing that the essence of AI Infra optimization lies in using mathematical equivalent transformations and precision trade-offs to achieve hardware efficiency.

relatedArticles.title: Beyond Cognitive Reconstruction: Stepping into the Engineering Revolution of Agentic Engineering
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep dive into the practical journey of Tencent engineers transitioning from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering, proposing an AI-assisted engineering system centered on context management and tool-oriented design.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: Can AI Write Code in Truly "Mission-Critical" Backend Systems?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article shares the complete methodology—Harness Engineering—practiced by Tencent's CDN LEGO team for AI coding in ultra-large-scale, high-reliability backend systems. Through a five-layer architecture, three key levers (context, constraints, feedback), and multi-model adversarial code review, they built an engineering system that enables AI to safely and controllably produce high-quality code.

relatedArticles.title: When the Entire Team Goes Zero-Manual Coding: A 10,000-Word AI-Native Development Handbook
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the Tencent team's practical experience in transitioning from AI-assisted programming to an AI-native development model, achieving a 'zero-manual coding' development loop through the OpenSpec specification and CodeBuddy toolchain.

relatedArticles.title: Kimi's New Paper: Turning KV Cache into a New Business Model
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Moonshot AI and Tsinghua University jointly propose the Prefill-as-a-Service architecture, which compresses the KV Cache through hybrid attention models, enabling its transmission across data centers via standard Ethernet, thereby achieving geo-distributed heterogeneous scheduling of Prefill and Decode, significantly improving long-context reasoning performance.
